LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard packaging conventions for a CMake-based KDE project. The source is a tarball fetched from the package's own declared upstream URL (github.com/ruizhi-lab/latte-dock-ng) at the version-tagged release, and it is protected by a real SHA-256 checksum, so there is no untrusted or mutable build-time fetch.

The build() function only configures and compiles the project with cmake, and package() only runs `cmake --install` under DESTDIR plus plain `cp -a`/`mkdir -p` operations that copy the project's own plasmoid, shell, separator, and indicator resources into the package directory. There are no network calls, no curl/wget, no eval or base64 decoding, no post-install hooks, and no modifications outside the package's own scope.

No injected code, exfiltration, backdoors, or attacker-controlled execution paths were found. The dependency list (KDE Frameworks, Qt6, Wayland) is consistent with the stated purpose of a Plasma dock.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard CMake PKGBUILD from declared upstream with valid checksum; no threats.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
